question.prompt: The parabolas \(y = ax^2 - 2\) and \(y = 4 - bx^2\) intersect the coordinate axes in exactly four points, and these four points are the vertices of a kite of area \(12.\) What is \(a + b?\)

solutions.explanation:
The printed conditions do not determine a unique value of \(a+b\). To see the missing condition, first determine the four vertices.

The two \(y\)-intercepts are \((0,-2)\) and \((0,4)\). Since both formulas depend on \(x^2\), any \(x\)-intercepts occur in a symmetric pair. Exactly four distinct combined axis-intersection points therefore means that the other two vertices are \((-t,0)\) and \((t,0)\), where \(t>0\).

Split the kite along its horizontal diagonal. The two triangles have common base \(2t\) and heights \(2\) and \(4\), so
\[
12=\frac12(2t)(2)+\frac12(2t)(4)=6t.
\]
Thus \(t=2\), and the horizontal vertices are \((\pm2,0)\).

Because the graphs are parabolas, \(a\ne0\) and \(b\ne0\). The first parabola crosses the \(x\)-axis exactly when \(a>0\), and the second does so exactly when \(b>0\). This gives three possible cases:

If \(a>0\) and \(b>0\), both must pass through \((2,0)\). Hence \(4a-2=0\) and \(4-4b=0\), giving \(a=\tfrac12\), \(b=1\), and \(a+b=\tfrac32\).

If \(a>0\) and \(b<0\), only the first parabola crosses the \(x\)-axis. Then \(a=\tfrac12\), while \(b\) can be any negative real number.

If \(a<0\) and \(b>0\), only the second parabola crosses the \(x\)-axis. Then \(b=1\), while \(a\) can be any negative real number. Both coefficients cannot be negative, because that would give only the two \(y\)-intercepts.

Every listed case gives the same four kite vertices. Consequently,
\[
a+b\in(-\infty,1)\cup\left\{\frac32\right\}.
\]
For example, \((a,b)=(-1,1)\) gives sum \(0\), while \((-2,1)\) gives sum \(-1\). Thus no unique value follows as written. Under the additional assumption \(a,b>0\), the answer is \(\boxed{1.5}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
solutions.title: Find the intercepts and check all coefficient signs
